introduction_strategy.hook_hypothesis: LLM repair tools return a patch and a statement that it works; users trust such statements (Perry 2023; Parasuraman 2010).
introduction_strategy.problem_gap_hypothesis: Benchmarks report how many repairs succeed, not how often a positive claim is false; the verification steps people add (gates, LLM juries, model-written tests, retrieval) are rarely measured against an executable oracle together with their cost.
research_questions: RQ3 executable evidence and localization rule, confirmed on unused cases
RQ4 retrieval for a cheaper model and cost per verified repair

points: RQ1: FAR stays high (43-66%) with a strong model; most failures pass functional tests but not exploit tests
RQ2: gate and jury did not lower FAR; jury multiplied cost
RQ3: model-written exploit tests did not lower FAR; the localization rule did, confirmed, at the price of correct claims; hint = footprint of the official fix
RQ4: retrieval did not raise the VRR of Claude Haiku 5.5 (13.8% vs. 14.9%, p = 0.73); its FAR was about 77%; the coverage rule held for it
v6 plan (waits until the retrieval step is tuned, since H1 was not confirmed)
